title: Frozen Shoulder Exercises: What to Do (and Avoid) at Each Stage
metaDescription: Frozen shoulder exercises explained simply: three easy stretches, how gently to do them, and when injections or surgery are considered.
intro: Gentle, regular stretching helps a frozen shoulder, and forcing it through pain does not. Frozen shoulder can take up to three years to settle, so the aim is to keep the movement you have and slowly regain more. Your doctor or physiotherapist should set your plan.

sections.heading: Do exercises help frozen shoulder?
sections.body: Yes. OrthoInfo says physiotherapists supervise exercises or give a home programme. Exercises do not cure it quickly, but they help keep the shoulder moving. Doing nothing lets it stiffen more.

sections.heading: What are the stages?
sections.body: Freezing (painful and stiffening), frozen (stiff, less painful) and thawing (movement slowly returning). OrthoInfo gives freezing as 6 weeks to 9 months, frozen about 4 to 6 months, and thawing 6 months to 2 years. Every shoulder is different.

sections.heading: What are three simple stretches?
sections.body: OrthoInfo describes these. Do them smoothly, never jerking.
bullets: Doorway turn: stand in a doorway, elbow bent at 90 degrees, and gently turn your body away; hold 30 seconds.
Lying lift: lie on your back, lift the sore arm overhead with the good arm; hold 15 seconds.
Cross-body stretch: pull the sore arm across your chest with the other hand; hold 30 seconds.

sections.heading: How hard should I push?
sections.body: Not into pain. OrthoInfo says to stretch only to a gentle stretch. Warmth before stretching can help. In the painful early stage, keep it very gentle and short. As the shoulder eases, you can hold a little longer and do more.

sections.heading: When do injections or surgery come in?
sections.body: If exercises and pain relief are not enough. Options include steroid injections into the joint, a stretching injection under imaging guidance (hydrodilatation), and keyhole surgery or gentle manipulation under anaesthesia. Surgery is usually considered only if there is no improvement after several months of treatment.

sections.heading: When should I see a doctor early?
sections.body: If the pain started after a fall or injury, if the arm is weak rather than stiff, if there is fever, redness or swelling, or if night pain is severe. If you have diabetes, tell your doctor, as it makes frozen shoulder more likely and can make it last longer.

faqs.q: How long does frozen shoulder last?
faqs.a: Up to about three years, though many are much better sooner.
